title: Two Vectors, North-of-East / South-of-East Example (Perpendicular Resultant)
notes: **If two vectors of equal magnitude 2 m act perpendicular to each other, find the resultant.** Let $|\vec{A}|=|\vec{B}|=2\,\text{m}$, $\theta=90°$: $R=\sqrt{A^2+B^2+2AB\cos\theta}=\sqrt{2^2+2^2+0}=\sqrt8=2\sqrt2\,\text{m}$.

Direction: $\tan\alpha=B/A=1 \Rightarrow \alpha=45°$, i.e. the resultant lies exactly midway between the two original vectors (e.g. if one points north-of-east and the other south-of-east, the resultant points due east).
Two vectors of magnitude 2 m at right angles have resultant sqrt(2^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(8) = 2√2 m, about 2.83 m. The cosine term is zero because the angle is 90°.
The direction from either vector is given by tanα = 2/2 = 1, so α = 45°. The resultant is midway between them.
Place one vector 45° north of east and the other 45° south of east. They are perpendicular, they have equal magnitude, and east is their bisector.
The northward component of the first is 2 sin45°, and the southward component of the second is the same size. Those components cancel.
confusion: 2√2 is not 4. The vectors are not parallel.
North of east and south of east are perpendicular only for this 45° choice, not for every pair of those phrases.
Cancelling the north and south parts does not cancel the eastward parts.
keyPoints: Equal 2 m vectors at 90° give 2√2 m.
North-of-east and south-of-east can be symmetric about east.
The resultant is then due east.

exercises.question: Two vectors, each of magnitude 2 m, point 45° north of east and 45° south of east. Find the resultant.
steps: The angle between them is 90°, and the magnitudes are equal.
The northward and southward components are equal and cancel.
The eastward components add to 2√2 m.
The resultant is 2√2 m due east.

summary: Equal vectors at right angles have resultant 2√2 m when each is 2 m, directed along the bisector. For the symmetric north-of-east and south-of-east pair, that bisector is due east because the sideways components cancel.
